liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (3 reviews): The jam out of Space into Iko Iko is mostly Bob and Jerry, and the reviewer ranks it among the coolest; The Space into Iko Iko transition is named as the high point of the show [7][8][18]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the jam linking China Cat into Rider the best version they have heard; China Cat into Rider opens the second set, with six songs before drums, signalling a hot set [7][9]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Bird Song in the first set is singled out as rocking [9]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): At the end of I Know You Rider, Phil blew out one of his stage monitors [11]
- **High Time** (1 review): Jerry's voice sounds sweet and full of passion on High Time [14]

## The recordings

- **gd82-09-14.beyer-sbd.miller.20906.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 156 min; rated 4.25/5 by 24 [1]. Said about its sound: First set is very well played and sounds good; Audience tape is called essential because it captures sounds filling every corner of the arena; Audience recording of the first set is praised; the second half circulates as soundboard [7][9][13][14]
- **gd1982-09-14.146663.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: source not stated; 23 songs; 154 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1982-09-14.155665.sbd.set1p.set2.patched.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 17 songs; 117 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [5]
- **gd1982-09-14.121943.akg414.streeter.miller.flac24**: source not stated; 23 songs; 152 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [3]

## Around the show

- Small, sweaty gym on a Tuesday night; stage set up lengthwise, making the room cozy with plenty of eye contact [11]
- Reviewer worked security as a student-athlete for University Union; it was their first Dead show [12]
- Reviewer's friend 'Moke, a friend of Bill Walton, helped them out [12]
- Reviewer attended this show at their alma mater, and had heard it was at Memorial Gymnasium rather than University Hall [17]
- Hot night; reviewer stood pressed close to the stage [18]
- Only time the Dead played Charlottesville; the show was booked by Chris Munson and Al Hinton [18]
- Not heavily jammed, unlike 30-minute Dark Stars, but samples a bit of everything, so it suits newcomers [8]
- Reviewer, who saw 140 Dead shows, calls this easily their favorite [11]
- Night reminded the reviewer of the Iowa Field House show the month before, perhaps because of the lineup [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd82-09-14.beyer-sbd.miller.20906.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [1]. Also: Second-set soundboard is posted separately; reviewer suggests trimming it from the matrix to get the first-set audience; First set: Beyer M160 to Sony D5 cassette master, then DAT, CD, EAC, SHN; Second set: soundboard to cassette master, reel, DAT, CD, EAC, SHN [1][17]
- **gd1982-09-14.146663.beyer.tompkins.flac2448**: taped by Rip Tompkins; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Source: FOB Beyers M88's > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell XLIIS-90 (1st Set, He's Gone, and JBGoode) and TDK MA-90 (2nd Set). Concert recording by Rip Tompkins, & with… [2]. Also: This version matches and upgrades the first-set recording in ID-20906; Left channel crossfaded over right at the starts of Samson and High Time; ID-121943 patches He's Gone [2]
- **gd1982-09-14.155665.sbd.set1p.set2.patched.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 7, 2022; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette > DAT (44.1k) [5]. Also: Patch source credited to Frank Streeter and Dan Healy; pitch-correction settings came from Joe B. Jones [5]
- **gd1982-09-14.121943.akg414.streeter.miller.flac24**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: AKG 414 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell XLII-S/TDK MA-R) [3]
